title: Mind ladder: most F1 concepts can never climb past Recall/Apply — 5 of 16 concepts have no route to any rung above Recall, only 3 can reach Evaluate
detail: The ladder (invariant 137) is derived from four evidence sources: Explain = an explain-back on a lesson whose `main` is the concept, or a checkpoint rubric row; Apply = a check/checkpoint item marked `apply` for the concept; Evaluate = a position on a contested lesson teaching the concept, or an Evaluate rubric row. Enumerating F1's authored content against those rules: premise, deduction, straw-man, false-dilemma and bandwagon have NO Explain, Apply or Evaluate source (they can only ever reach Recall); conclusion, soundness, ad-hominem, slippery-slope reach Recall+Apply only; standard-form has Explain but no Apply; steelman has no Explain (F1.7 is contested, so its prompt is a position). Only induction, charity and steelman can reach Evaluate. Yet every met concept is drawn with four rungs, the desk hero shows 'Evaluate 0%' bars computed over all met concepts and 'furthest' needs half the met concepts on a rung — so a learner who does every piece of F1 perfectly still sees Explain ≈ 38%, Evaluate ≈ 19% and four-rung ladders that cannot be completed, with no hint why.
evidence: eval over KOS_MIND (slot 11): 'premise E[] A[] V[]', 'deduction E[] A[] V[]', 'straw-man E[] A[] V[]', 'false-dilemma E[] A[] V[]', 'bandwagon E[] A[] V[]', 'soundness E[] A[F1.3#2] V[]', 'standard-form E[F1.2] A[] V[]', 'steelman E[] A[F1.7#1] V[F1.7,cp]'; rules in js/core/mind.js:278-318 (ladder); hero bars js/modules/mind.js:66-72; furthest js/core/mind.js:497-503
fix: Either author a route for every rung of every concept (apply items for each fallacy/premise/deduction; explain-back key points or checkpoint rubric rows for the rest), or let a concept declare which rungs it has (`rungs: ['Recall','Apply']`) and draw/count only those, computing the hero bars and 'furthest' over reachable rungs. smoke110 should assert every concept has a source for every rung it shows.
rootCause: Ladder rules require per-concept evidence sources that the F1 content file only provides for the lesson 'main' concepts; nothing checks reachability.

title: Inspector 'Ask Kurenai' grid: 'Explain it differently' overflows its button's padding at mac width
detail: On a Mind lesson at 1470px the inspector's Ask Kurenai grid is two 118.5px columns; the 'Explain it differently' label (nowrap) is 116px wide, so it spills over the 14px side paddings and touches the pill's border on both sides, unlike the other three chips.

title: The F1 checkpoint lesson (F1.8) can never reach Completed: its fourth check reads retrieval over the lesson's concepts, and a checkpoint lesson has none
detail: A lesson without a written prompt has three checks and its fourth slot is 'all three hold' (js/core/mind.js:347-355). For a checkpoint lesson the third evidence check is `retrieval`, computed over `l.concepts` (js/core/mind.js:338-340) — but F1.8 is registered with `concepts: []` (its concepts live on KOS_MIND.CHECKPOINTS.F1.concepts). So retrieval is always false and the shared progress record never gets checks 3–4: after the page is read, the checkpoint is passed and every one of the checkpoint's concepts' cards is rated Good, F1.8 stays 'started' with check [true,true,false,false]. Consequences: the unit can never show 8/8 completed, Mind mastery can never reach 100% (F1.8 caps at 2/3), the desk's 'Lessons' tile tops out at 7/8, and anything reading `completed` (unitState.completed, achievements, Reports) under-counts.
evidence: eval (slot 11): after recordCheckpoint('F1'), markPage('F1.8',0) and rateCard(...,3) on argument and induction cards → evidence('F1.8').checks [true,true,null,false], peekProgress('mind','F1.8') {status:'started', check:[true,true,false,false]}, completed('F1.8') false, KOS_MIND.LESSONS['F1.8'].concepts []
fix: In evidence(), for a checkpoint lesson read the concepts from M().CHECKPOINTS[l.unit].concepts (or its cards) — or treat the checkpoint itself (cards step) as its retrieval; add a smoke110 case that a fully done checkpoint lesson reaches status done.
rootCause: evidence() derives 'retrieval' from l.concepts, which the checkpoint lesson registration leaves empty (js/data/content/mind-f1.js checkpoint lesson)

title: Evaluate is lost whenever a position is revised: the revise sheet starts with an empty objection/reply and the ladder reads only the latest version
detail: ladder() grants Evaluate from `latest(lid)` having both objection and reply (js/core/mind.js:308-312). The position sheet pre-fills answer, confidence and reason from the previous version but always starts objection and reply as '' (js/modules/mindrun.js:96 `objection: "", reply: ""`), and the objection <details> is closed. So a learner who answered an objection in v1 and later revises (e.g. a revisit's 'Revise', or nudging confidence) without retyping it drops the concept back below Evaluate — for every concept the contested lesson teaches (F1.7: steelman AND charity). The saved card then shows the ladder without Evaluate and no message says it was lost. An 'earned' rung going away on an unrelated edit contradicts 'every rung comes from evidence' (the earlier evidence still exists in version history).
evidence: eval (slot 11): takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,objection:'o',reply:'y'}) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] true, ladder('charity').rungs[3] true; then takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,conf:60,reason:'r2'}) (what the revise sheet sends when the objection is not retyped) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] false
fix: Evaluate should hold if ANY version (or any non-retired position) has an objection answered; and pre-fill the revise sheet's objection/reply from the previous version (open the details when present).
rootCause: ladder uses only the latest version; position() sheet does not carry the objection forward

title: Checkpoint pays 50 XP / 12 gold / +4 HP and marks itself passed with nothing right; a retake then erases the Explain/Evaluate rungs it gave
detail: recordCheckpoint() always sets doneAt and pays the first time (js/core/mind.js:382-405); the UI's only gate is one non-empty synthesis bullet (js/modules/mind.js:562). Cards are self-marked 'Had it/Not quite' and apply scenarios can all be wrong — 0 of 8 cards, 0 of 3 scenarios, 0 rubric points and a one-character bullet still pay the full checkpoint reward and tick F1.8's 'Check passed'. (Japanese's checkpoint requires 80% in every skill; the Mind plan's 'unit checkpoint 50/12/+4' reads as a passed checkpoint.) Separately, Retake overwrites `apply` and `synth.ticks` wholesale, so a retake with fewer rubric ticks removes Explain (argument, hidden-premise) and Evaluate (induction, steelman) that the first attempt earned.
evidence: eval (slot 11): recordCheckpoint('F1',{cards:0,apply:{},synth:{bullets:['x'],ticks:{0:true,2:true}}}) → {paid:true}, governor 0/0 → 50/12; ledger [F1.8,{kind:'checkpoint',first:true},{xp:50,gold:12}]; ladder('argument').rungs[1] true, ladder('induction').rungs[3] true; retake recordCheckpoint('F1',{synth:{bullets:['y'],ticks:{}}}) → both false
fix: Define a pass rule (e.g. ≥ 2 of 3 scenarios right and ≥ half the rubric) and pay only on the first PASS, saying what is missing otherwise; keep the best attempt (merge apply/ticks by OR, or store attempts and read the best) so a retake never lowers a rung.
rootCause: recordCheckpoint has no pass condition and replaces the record on every attempt

title: Apply and Explain rungs are earned without showing understanding: Apply after the check has revealed the answer, Explain from one one-character bullet
detail: Leniency of the derived ladder with thin evidence: (1) Apply = 'a scenario answered right'. A wrong answer immediately marks the right option '✓ Right' (js/modules/mindtopic.js:103-106) and offers 'Next, and come back to this'; coming back, clicking the option that was just revealed records ok:true (answerCheck keeps the first ok) and the concept reaches Apply — so every Apply rung (and the check pass that pays 12 XP) can be had by guessing once. (2) Explain = ≥60% of key points self-ticked; the text itself is not checked at all, so a single bullet 'x' with 3 of 4 ticks reaches Explain, and the explain-back can be written before a single page is read.
evidence: eval (slot 11): answerCheck('F1.3',3,0) → ok:false, ladder('validity').apply 0; answerCheck('F1.3',3,1) → ok:true, apply 1, rungs [F,F,T,F]; saveExplain('F1.3',['x'],{0:1,1:1,2:1}) → {reached:true,ticked:3,of:4} with evidence('F1.3').read 0 of 6
fix: Count Apply only when the scenario is right at the FIRST attempt of a visit (or on a later day, with the answer not revealed in the same session); for a retried item show 'Right, but it counts next time'. For Explain require a minimum (e.g. ≥ 3 bullets or ~20 words) before ticks count, and order the prompt after the pages.
rootCause: answerCheck records ok on any later right answer; saveExplain trusts ticks with no text threshold

title: Mind desk on iPhone and iPad portrait: the Daily 15 and Continue cards are crushed to 40px — the Start button, the plan and the lesson title are cut off
detail: Below 1080px the shared desk rule gives every side card `flex: 1 1 0` (css/views/study.css:1076) and the study-space rule gives them `min-block-size: 0; overflow: hidden` (study.css:55). Japanese and Creatives turn their side column into a grid (japanese.css:449, creatives.css:366), but Mind's side is `display:flex; flex-direction:column` (css/views/mind.css:112), so in an auto-height column each card's basis is 0 and it collapses to its padding: the Daily 15 card is 40px tall with 189px of content, its '▶ Start' button sits 129px below the card's clipped bottom, and Continue shows only its kicker and half the → circle. The desk's main call to action is invisible on two of the user's three devices. On the Mac the same clipping cuts the Daily card's button in Exam Season (card 191px, content 254px: the '▶ Reviews · 5 min' button at y=340 is below the card's bottom at 333), because the side column is held to the hero's height.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-desk-iphone-daily.png; eval (seeded, Exam Season stubbed off): ipad cardH 40 scrollH 189, Start bottom 873 vs card bottom 744; iphone cardH 40 scrollH 189, Start bottom 747 vs card bottom 618; mac (Exam Season on) card 191.6px, scrollHeight 254, overflow hidden, button top 340
fix: Give .k-mind-deskside the same treatment as Japanese/Creatives under 1080px (grid, or flex-basis auto), and on the Mac let the Daily card's content set a minimum (min-block-size: min-content) or drop the strip/blurb before the button rather than clipping the button; add the Mind desk to smoke/visual audit at 820 and 402.
devices: iphone, ipad portrait (all states); mac in Exam Season
rootCause: Mind's side column overrides the shared side layout with a flex column that, combined with flex:1 1 0 and min-block-size:0/overflow:hidden, collapses its children

title: Exam Season Daily 15 with no cards due still offers '▶ Reviews · 5 min', which ends instantly as 'Done for today. 1 minute.'
detail: In Exam Season planDay() returns reviews {n:0, min:0}, sitting null, question null, total 0 — but the desk card still says 'Reviews only until your exams end.' with an '≈ 5 min' chip, and the Daily page lists 'Reviews · No cards due · ~5′' with a primary '▶ Reviews · 5 min' button. Pressing it starts a Focus stopwatch and jumps straight to done: 'Done for today. 1 minute.', stamping today's Daily as done though nothing was done (and the 1 minute is invented: d.mins = max(1, …)). The '≈ 5 min' chip is hard-coded on p.exam rather than read from plan.total.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-mind-daily-mac.png; eval: planDay() {exam:true,reviews:{n:0,min:0},total:0}; after clicking: #main text 'Done for today. 1 minute.', ui.mind.daily {step:'done',mins:1,doneAt:…}; chip js/modules/mind.js:126 (p.exam ? '≈ 5 min'), intro js/modules/mind.js:640-647, stopFocus mins js/modules/mind.js:617

title: Dialogue 'Skip to summary' on the first question gives an empty '0 turns' summary, and 'Save to Journal' saves an empty Reflection (counted by the Journal badge)
detail: In a Socratic dialogue, 'Skip to summary' is offered from the very first node. Pressed there, the summary card reads 'THE LINE YOU TOOK · 0 TURNS' with no line at all, and its primary '≋ Save to Journal' writes a reflection titled 'Dialogue: …' with text '' to the Journal; the Badge Wall immediately pinged 'Journal 2 / 10 entries' for it. Every authored path is 3–5 turns (invariant 140), so a 0-turn summary is never meaningful.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-dialogue-0turns-mac.png; eval: KOS.mindJournal.list() → ['reflection','Dialogue: Is every disagreement an argument?',''] after the save; js/modules/mindrun.js:186-205 (onEnd builds the save button whatever the path length)

title: Ask Kurenai offline: 'Saved to ask when you're online. You will see "What is sent" again' — the queue is written and never read
detail: Pressing Send while offline pushes {lesson, concept, mode, typed} to state.ui.mind.askQueue and tells the learner it will be asked when they are back online, after showing What is sent again. Nothing in the codebase reads askQueue: the question is silently dropped (and the queue grows per device for ever). The Daily 15 card's offline line also promises 'Ask Kurenai waits for a connection'.
evidence: grep -rn askQueue js/ → only js/modules/mindrun.js:299-300 (write); message text js/modules/mindrun.js:303; js/modules/mind.js:136
fix: Either implement the queue (on 'online' or the next Mind open, show a 'You asked while offline' card that reopens the What is sent step for each queued item) or say plainly 'You're offline — try again when connected' and keep the typed words in the sheet.

title: Ask Kurenai's 'What is sent' pre-ticks the explain-back under 'Extras · tick to include', summarises instead of printing the payload, and says '1 bullets'
detail: On a lesson with an explain-back, extras.explain defaults to true (`|| !!ex`, js/modules/mindrun.js:233), so the learner's own writing is included unless they untick it — opposite of 'tick to include'. The list shows labels ('The concept and the lesson: Validity · F1.3') but the request also carries the concept's gist (and key points in check mode) and the explain-back text itself, which are not printed (invariant 140: sends only what What is sent shows; Reports' 102b prints the exact payload). The extra's sub-line reads '1 bullets'.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-ask-sent-mac.png; eval: checkbox [true, 'Your explain-back for this lesson 1 bullets']; payload() js/modules/mindrun.js:251-261 vs whatIsSent list :265-269; tick sub-line :277
fix: Default extras off (or keep the default but say 'included · untick to leave out'); add a 'Show the exact text' disclosure printing payload(); pluralise ('1 bullet').
rootCause: Extras default derived from existence of an explain-back; summary list built separately from payload()

title: Journal entries cannot be edited or linked to a concept after capture, though capture says 'Link a concept later'
detail: Quick capture saves kind, text and source with no concept (unless opened from a lesson) and says 'Link a concept later. Private: only you read it.' The Journal's entry card offers only 'Make it the Big Question' (questions), 'Ask Kurenai' and 'Delete' — no edit, no change of kind, no 'Link a concept'. A typo or a missing concept can only be fixed by deleting and recapturing (losing its date). The 'Concept: any' filter and the concept-filtered commonplace export therefore never find captured entries. The source field 'Source, for a quote' is also shown for every kind.
evidence: js/modules/mindrun.js:371 'Link a concept later'; entryCard js/modules/mind.js:316-341 (buttons); /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-journal2-mac.png
fix: Add an Edit action on each entry that reopens the capture sheet pre-filled (kind, text, source, concept chips from metConcepts) and saves through KOS.mindJournal.put (it already keeps id and bumps updatedAt for sync); show the source field only for Quote.
rootCause: No edit UI on top of the existing put()

title: Mind is barely joined to the rest of the OS: no Reports facts or milestones, Goals' card/recall types silently read 0 for Mind, and Home/Today never mention the Daily 15 or Mind cards due
detail: (1) Reports: js/core/report.js has no Mind facts at all (grep 'mind' → nothing), although docs/mind-plan.md:332 says milestones 'show on the desk and in Reports' and invariant 139 describes Reports counting Journal entries; Creatives has creativeFacts (report.js:644), Code programming(). Mind work appears only as anonymous Focus minutes. (2) Goals: the subject picker offers every KOS.subjects id including Mind (js/modules/goals.js:834), but 'Review flashcards' and 'Keep recall at or above' count only ledger types flashcards/due-review (js/core/goals.js:557-572), so 'Review flashcards · Mind' never moves — Mind reviews are logged as type 'mind' (js/core/mind.js:273). There is no Mind goal domain (DOMAINS goals.js:44 has code and creatives, not mind). (3) Home / Today: KOS.today.build() carries nothing from Mind (no Daily 15, no cards due, no revisit due), so the Daily 15 lives only on the Mind desk; the Morning/Evening reviews and Home's 'Today's three' never surface it.
evidence: grep -rln 'KOS.mind' js/ → only ui, aitools, achcatalogue, achievements, governor, art, subjects, hub, governor-ui (no report.js, goals.js, today.js, dayreview.js); eval: JSON of KOS.today.build() contains no 'mind'/'Mind' field (only 'reminder' substrings); goals.js:557-572 type filter
fix: Add mindFacts to report.js (reviews passed, lessons finished, checkpoints, positions taken/changed, Journal counts — totals only), let cards-reviewed/recall-rate read type 'mind' review entries when the subject is Mind (or hide Mind from those pickers), and give KOS.today a Mind item (Daily 15 not done / cards due / revisit due) through KOS.mind.planDay.
rootCause: Mind shipped as a self-contained space; the joins listed in the plan were not built

title: Checkpoint Argument Mapper: every claim starts as 'conclusion', the warning says 'Two conclusions' for five, and an untouched map still earns 'First argument mapped'
detail: The map step seeds every claim at depth 0 with no joint, so all five rows are labelled 'conclusion'. The warning is hard-coded 'Two conclusions: is that right?' whatever the count (5 here). 'Next · the synthesis' accepts the map as it is, and milestones() counts any stored map as 'First argument mapped' (js/core/mind.js:509) — so pressing Next without moving anything earns the milestone. Nothing compares the learner's map with the model map (only an optional 'Compare' sheet).
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/mind/s-cp-map-ipad.png; js/core/mindui.js:202 (fixed text); js/modules/mind.js:537 (rows seeded d:0, j:null) and :545 (Next stores mp.value())
fix: Word the warning from the count ('5 conclusions — only one claim is the conclusion'); start rows unplaced (a neutral 'claim' label) and count the milestone only when the map has exactly one top row and every other row has a joint.
rootCause: Static warning text; milestone reads presence of r.map
